q_goods_transfer.text: Does the contract involve execution of work together with transfer of property in goods (materials incorporated into the work), rather than the supply of skill/labour alone?
q_goods_transfer.legal_test: State of Madras v. Gannon Dunkerley & Co., AIR 1958 SC 560 and Art. 366(29A) Constitution: a works contract is a composite contract for work-and-materials involving transfer of property in goods; a pure service contract transfers no goods.

q_deliverable.text: Is the deliverable the worked-upon/fabricated property itself (e.g. construction, fabrication, installation on immovable property), as opposed to an incidental use of materials during a predominantly-service engagement?
q_deliverable.legal_test: Dominant-intention / predominant-nature test: where the substance is execution of works with materials, the instrument is a works contract; where materials are merely incidental to a service, it is a service agreement.

grey_mixed.reason: Materials are present but the predominant nature (works vs service) is genuinely mixed. Classification affects duty — apply S.6 highest-duty and recommend adjudication (S.31) rather than guessing.

source.ref: State of Madras v. Gannon Dunkerley & Co., AIR 1958 SC 560; Constitution Art. 366(29A); Indian Stamp Act 1899 Sch. I-A Art. 5 & s.6
source.quoted_text: A works contract is a composite work-and-materials contract involving transfer of property in goods; a service agreement supplies skill/labour without transfer of goods. Where the predominant nature is unclear, s.6 charges the highest of the competing duties.

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on the legal tests.
